title: Coalition-Aware Skill Reliability for Self-Evolving Agents
abstract: arXiv:2608.22610v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agent skills, structured artifacts distilled from interaction trajectories and dynamically reused from skill banks, have become a central mechanism for enabling large language model (LLM)-based self-evolving agents to learn from past experience. Yet existing work has largely focused on the operational aspects of skills, such as acquisition, evolution, and retrieval, while leaving a more fundamental reliability question unresolved: Do accumulated skills in an agent's skill bank actually make positive mechanistic contributions? We investigate this question through systematic skill-bank audits across alternative bank compositions and deployment domains, measuring the resulting changes in agent behavior. These audits reveal two recurring reliability failures: coalition pollution, where bank-level gains conceal negative coalition-level skill contributions, and cross-domain utility reversal, where source-beneficial skills reverse their effects

translated_title: 联盟感知的技能可靠性用于自进化智能体
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.22610v1 公告类型：新 摘要：智能体技能，作为从交互轨迹中提炼的结构化产物并从技能库中动态重用，已成为使基于大型语言模型（LLM）的自进化智能体从过往经验中学习的关键机制。然而，现有工作主要集中于技能的操作层面，如获取、进化和检索，却留下了一个更基本的可靠性问题未解决：智能体技能库中积累的技能是否真正产生积极的机制性贡献？我们通过系统性的技能库审计，跨越不同的库组成和部署领域，测量由此产生的智能体行为变化来探究这一问题。这些审计揭示了两种反复出现的可靠性失败：联盟污染，即库级收益掩盖了负面的联盟级技能贡献；以及跨领域效用反转，即源领域有益的技能效果发生逆转。
tldr: 本文通过系统性审计发现，智能体技能库中存在联盟污染和跨领域效用反转两类可靠性问题，强调技能贡献需以联盟感知方式评估。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals through systematic audits that agent skill banks suffer from coalition pollution and cross-domain utility reversal, emphasizing the need for coalition-aware reliability assessment of skill contributions.
